featured_reviews.name: VSK
featured_reviews.review_text:
INHS Asvini, also known as Indian Naval Hospital Ship Asvini, is a premier healthcare facility of the Indian Navy located in Mumbai, India. It serves as a tertiary care hospital and provides medical services primarily to serving and retired personnel of the Indian Navy and their dependents. Here is a review of INHS Asvini based on its services and facilities.

INHS Asvini is a well-equipped hospital with state-of-the-art medical infrastructure and modern facilities. The hospital offers a wide range of medical services, including general medicine, surgery, pediatrics, gynecology, orthopedics, ophthalmology, and dentistry. It has well-equipped operation theaters, intensive care units, diagnostic imaging facilities, and a blood bank, ensuring comprehensive healthcare services.

The hospital is staffed by highly skilled and experienced medical professionals, including doctors, nurses, and support staff. The medical staff at INHS Asvini is known for their expertise, professionalism, and commitment to patient care. They provide quality medical treatment and strive to ensure the well-being of the patients.

INHS Asvini is known for its efficient emergency services. The hospital has a dedicated emergency department that operates round the clock, providing immediate medical assistance to patients in critical conditions. The emergency department is equipped to handle various medical emergencies and has an ambulance service for swift patient transport.

The hospital also focuses on preventive healthcare and has specialized clinics and departments for various health concerns. These include lifestyle diseases, cardiology, dermatology, psychiatry, physiotherapy, and nutrition. INHS Asvini conducts regular health check-up camps and awareness programs to promote a healthy lifestyle among its beneficiaries.

The infrastructure of INHS Asvini is well-maintained and clean. The hospital premises are spacious, allowing for ease of movement for patients and visitors. The waiting areas are comfortable and provide a serene environment for patients and their attendants.

INHS Asvini is committed to patient welfare and provides various support services to enhance the overall experience. These include a pharmacy, laboratory services, counseling services, and a canteen facility. The hospital also has tie-ups with reputed medical institutions and specialists for referrals and advanced treatment options.

One aspect that could be improved is the waiting time for certain services, especially during peak hours. Like any busy hospital, INHS Asvini experiences heavy patient load, which can lead to longer waiting times for consultations and procedures. However, the hospital management continuously strives to streamline processes and reduce waiting times.

In summary, INHS Asvini is a highly regarded healthcare facility catering to the medical needs of the Indian Navy personnel and their dependents. With its comprehensive medical services, modern infrastructure, skilled medical professionals, and focus on patient care, the hospital provides quality healthcare services. While waiting times can be a concern during peak hours, INHS Asvini remains a trusted and reliable healthcare institution, upholding the commitment to the health and well-being of the naval community it serves.

It was so frustrating that I had to make my mother travel everytime for absolutely no reason just because the staff is highly incompetent. Absolutely inhumane and unprofessional attitude by the department. All 3 times, I had to take my ill mother but they didn't even bother to see her or talk to her or advise us anything. I’m writing this review with a broken heart. My mother-in-law is no longer with us, and I believe DR. SALMAN ALI SAYED (Nephrologist) at this hospital is responsible.
He misdiagnosed her condition - or failed to diagnose it properly at all. Her health deteriorated rapidly under his care. What could have been treated became fatal because of medical negligence.
We trusted this doctor with someone we loved. We believed he would help her. Instead, we lost her.
The rushed appointments, the failure to listen to our concerns, the lack of proper and unnecessary testing - it all added up to a tragedy that didn’t have to happen. This hospital treated her like a SOURCE of REVENUE, not a HUMAN BEING fighting for her life.
She’s gone now. Our family is shattered. And I have to live every day knowing that better care could have saved her.

To anyone reading this:

PLEASE get a second opinion. Ask questions. Demand answers. Don’t trust blindly like we did.

If this review saves even one person from what we went through, then maybe her death won’t be completely meaningless.

We will never get her back. Don’t let this happen to your family.

I am from Chhattisgarh and suddenly developed severe imbalance to the extent that I was unable to stand properly. On the advice of our family neuro physician, we immediately consulted Dr. Arvind Kulkarni, a highly reputed neurosurgeon known to us through successful surgeries of our acquaintances.
After examining me and reviewing my MRI, Dr. Kulkarni advised immediate surgery. We chose Breach Candy Hospital because of its excellent reputation. The surgery was successfully performed on 28th March, and throughout the entire process, we received exceptional care and guidance.
The hospital facilities, especially the Super Deluxe Room arrangements, were outstanding. The nursing staff, paramedical team, and housekeeping staff were extremely caring, courteous, and professional.
Dr. Kulkarni’s counseling, clarity of explanation, patience in answering every query, and reassuring approach before and after surgery were remarkable. I would also especially like to thank Dr. Janardhan, a wonderful doctor and compassionate human being, who closely monitored my recovery and explained every detail with great care and positivity.
Today, I am able to stand on my feet again, and for that, my heartfelt gratitude goes to Dr. Kulkarni, Dr. Janardhan, and the entire team of Breach Candy Hospital. We shall always remain grateful for the excellent treatment and humane care provided to us.

featured_reviews.name: Mohammed Abdul Raouf
featured_reviews.review_text:
Grant Medical College, established in 1845, is one of the oldest and most premier medical institutions in South Asia. It is consistently ranked among the top 10 medical colleges in India. Attached to the massive Sir J.J. Group of Hospitals, it serves as a tertiary care referral center for the entire state of Maharashtra.
The Strengths (Pros)
* Unmatched Clinical Exposure: This is the college's biggest selling point. The associated J.J. Hospital has a massive patient inflow (thousands of outpatients daily). As a student, you will see rare cases and common diseases in abundance. By the time you finish your internship, your clinical skills will be far superior to students from most other colleges.
* Top-Tier Faculty: The professors are often leaders in their respective fields. Being a government college in Mumbai, it attracts the best medical teachers.
* Affordability: Being a state government college, the fee structure is heavily subsidized and very affordable compared to private institutions.
* Location: Located in Byculla (South Mumbai), the campus is in the heart of the city. It is well-connected by local trains (Byculla station is walking distance) and offers access to the best of Mumbai.
* Prestige & Alumni Network: Graduating from "Grant" carries significant weight in the medical community, both in India and abroad (US/UK). The alumni network is vast and powerful.
The Challenges (Cons)
* Infrastructure & Maintenance: While the campus has beautiful heritage buildings, some facilities are aging. Lecture halls and labs are functional but may not be as modern or "glossy" as high-end private colleges.
* Hostel Conditions: This is a common complaint. Hostels can be crowded, and hygiene maintenance in the washrooms sometimes lags. Many students opt to live in PGs nearby after the first year, though this is expensive in South Mumbai.
* High Workload: The environment is high-pressure. Due to the massive patient load, internships and residency can be grueling with very long hours.
Campus Life
* Vibrant Atmosphere: The campus is huge (44 acres). It has a unique mix of medical students, nursing students, and physiotherapy students.
* Events: The annual cultural festival, "Astitva," and the sports meet, "Kurukshetra," are very popular and provide a much-needed break from studies.
* Gymkhana: There is a sprawling gymkhana ground (Marine Lines) associated with the college for sports enthusiasts.
Quick Summary Table
| Feature | Rating | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Academics | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Excellent teaching and case variety. |
| Clinical Exposure | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | World-class; arguably the best in Western India. |
| Infrastructure | ⭐⭐⭐ | Heritage buildings, but needs modernization. |
| Hostels | ⭐⭐ | Often crowded; needs renovation. |
| Fees | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Very economical (Govt. rates). |
Final Verdict
Grant Government Medical College is an excellent choice for students who prioritize clinical learning and hands-on experience over luxury infrastructure.
If you are willing to work hard and adjust to a heritage campus environment, this college will mold you into a highly competent doctor. It is ideal for those who want the "real" medical experience in the heart of Mumbai.

Today I came to Mumbai and it reminded me of this hospital. In 2024 I admitted my sister here but forgot to write the review. So here it is.

It was early morning and my sister had sudden pain in her stomach. Looking at the pain I was quite evident that it was due to stone. As we were near to Parakh hospital we reached there. As per doctor's advice ultrasound was done and as I thought it was due to stone only. We requested doctor to provide some medicine for getting relief from pain so that we can go back to Gwalior and we will take further treatment there as it is our hometown. But he insisted for getting admitted. Considering the pain we decided for getting admitted. They kept giving my sister injections and medicines for holding the pain. Also ran some other tests. After 24 hours they started insisting for surgery. We finally decided to get discharged from the hospital. The total expense that we had to pay for this 1 day was 30000/-
Worse part was that immediately after the discharge the pain returned and my sister was still in the same situation as 1 day before.
At last I went to a medical store nearby and told him about the pain. The medical store guy gave just 1 pill and with that medicine the entire pain vanished and my sister reached back Gwalior via train without any pain.
In Gwalior she took homeopathy medicine treatment and in six months all the stones are gone without any surgery.

So I'm not sure about how this hospital is at present but in October 2024 they literally looted us in just a single day. So beware.
